The printed six-line trace is reproduced line for line, including every C_max and C_min; switch multiset [1^11,2,4] with c_10 four times; strict variant 5 rounds, multiset [1^11]. Halting pair has L = U on all 16 controlled vertices with w*(c_1) = 11337633945805671/51622576448108128447, which equals the independent brute-force max over all 256 Max strategies of val_sigma. results.name: bsr:lem-bias (same-successor bias)
results.statement: If v in Vmax has successors p in Vmax and q in Vavg with the same successor pair {a,b}, then val^tau(p) >= val^tau(q) for every tau, with equality iff val^tau(a)=val^tau(b); so strict BSI never endorses p->q, non-strict endorses it only at equality, q->p is always endorsed when improving, and p->q is val_sigma-improving at v iff p is strictly switchable at sigma.
results.argument: val^tau is the value of the Max-only game with Min frozen, so val^tau(p) = max{val^tau(a),val^tau(b)} and val^tau(q) = (val^tau(a)+val^tau(b))/2: a maximum dominates a mean, with equality only when the arguments agree. The vetoes of def:bsi read off directly. Last clause: val_sigma(p) = val_sigma(sigma(p)) with sigma(p) in {a,b}, so val_sigma(q) > val_sigma(p) iff val_sigma(sigma-bar(p)) > val_sigma(sigma(p)).
results.verification: Two-line proof, checked. Computationally confirmed on all 15 configurations of this shape in the ladders L_n, n=2..6 (bsi_v.py) and on the 5 configurations that random search produced. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: bsr:prop-selfdual (BSI on a self-dual game is the one-sided rule MR)
results.statement: On a stopping self-dual G with involution phi, val^{phi(sigma)}(x) = 1 - val_sigma(phi(x)) for every x including the sinks; from a mirrored pair every BSI round produces a mirrored pair, C_min = phi(C_max), and C_max = {v in S_sigma : val_sigma(phi(sigma-bar(v))) <= val_sigma(phi(sigma(v)))} (< for the strict variant), so BSI collapses to the one-sided rule MR reading val_sigma and phi only.
results.argument: Freezing Min to phi(sigma) leaves a Max-only stopping game whose dual phi carries isomorphically onto G_sigma; lem:duality gives the identity off the sinks, and at the sinks both sides read 1 at t_1 and 0 at t_0 because phi exchanges them. Substituting U = 1 - L o phi into def:bsi turns S^{phi(sigma)} into phi(S_sigma) and the Min veto into the Max veto, so C_min = phi(C_max) and tau[C_min] = phi(sigma[C_max]).
results.verification: bsi_v.py: 60 random self-dual stopping games (built by choosing successors on one half and mirroring), both variants, WHOLE trajectories -- the identity checked at every vertex including sinks, C_min = phi(C_max) at every round, the mirrored-pair invariance after every update, and the identification with MR at every round. 0 violations. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: bsr:prop-normal (normalisation preserves the BSI trajectory)
results.statement: For the bipartite normal form N'(G) of lem:normalform, val_{sigma~} = val_sigma and val^{tau~} = val^tau on V(G) with the value of u at both gadget vertices; hence S, S^tau, C_max, C_min and the whole BSI run coincide, for both variants; likewise for N_k of def:kblind.
results.argument: lem:normalform(iii) is the statement for val_sigma. The gadget uses only average vertices and is inserted exactly at the edges whose two endpoints are controlled -- a condition invariant under exchanging players and sinks -- so N'(G-bar) = the dual of N'(G) under the same naming; lem:normalform(iii) applied to G-bar and carried back by lem:duality is the statement for val^tau. Each of the four tests of def:bsi then compares two unchanged numbers.
results.verification: bsi_nf.py: N'(G) built from scratch (with the sinks carried as SENTINELS -- the first attempt collided the fresh vertex indices with t_0 and produced 149 spurious mismatches, which is exactly the trap the standing rules record), 40 random two-player stopping games, both variants, whole trajectories: identical lengths, identical C_max/C_min at every round, identical L and U on V(G), and both gadget vertices carrying val(u) for L and for U. 0 violations. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: deg:prop-hk5 (h*_HK(5) = 11)
results.statement: h*(m) = 1,2,4,7,12 and h*_HK(m) = 1,2,4,6,11 for m <= 5. No Holt-Klee AUSO of the 5-cube has BA height 12; the printed outmap (7,14,28,13,24,25,26,27,15,16,17,22,19,4,5,18,30,29,0,31,3,10,12,9,23,2,8,1,11,20,21,6) is a Holt-Klee AUSO of height 11 attained along 0->7->28->23->30->11->29->9->25->27->26->18; and prop:hstar-five's height-12 witness violates Holt-Klee on the 3-face with free directions {1,2,3} through sigma = 16.
results.argument: Every BA trace of an AUSO obeys cor:no-return, cor:law-b and cor:law-u, so an exhaustive DFS over law-abiding sequences enumerates a superset of the traces. NO Holt-Klee acyclic completion exists.

results.name: deg:prop-zeroties (damping cannot remove a tie at value zero)
results.statement: If G^flat replaces each edge u->w by a damping chain of arbitrary edge-dependent length k_e >= 0, then for every Max strategy sigma the zero set of val^{G^flat}_sigma on V(G) equals the zero set of val^G_sigma, namely the trapping set Z_sigma, which depends on the digraph and sigma alone. Hence every incidence tied at value 0 stays tied, whatever the k_e; in particular no such perturbation makes B' nondegenerate.
results.argument: By lem:trap it suffices to show that the greatest sigma-trap of G^flat meets V(G) in the greatest sigma-trap Z of G. (Superset) U := Z union {chain vertices of edges whose head lies in Z} is a sigma-trap of G^flat: an average chain vertex keeps both successors (the head, in Z, and the next chain vertex, or t_0 which lies in Z); an average v in Z has both G-successors in Z so both chain heads in U; a Max v in Z keeps sigma(v)'s chain head; a Min v in Z keeps some chain head; and t_1 is not in U. (Subset) W := Z^flat meet V(G) is a sigma-trap of G: a chain head in Z^flat is average, so BOTH its successors -- including the head w -- lie in Z^flat, giving both G-successors of an average v in W, and one successor of a controlled v in W. Finally, if both successors of a Max vertex have value 0 then both chain heads have value (1-2^{-k})*0 + 2^{-k}*0 = 0.
results.verification: Proof re-derived line by line; it is correct and holds for arbitrary SSGs with Min vertices present, and uses no probability. The last clause re-measured: B'_7 has exactly the ten ties {(1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(3,1),(3,2),(5,1),(5,2),(6,2),(7,1),(7,2)}, all at value 0, and under 400 random per-edge chain-length assignments in {7,...,13} the SAME ten incidences stay tied in all 400 (bprime.py). VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: allswlower:lem-isolated (no return to an isolated configuration)
results.statement: If S_t is contained in W then sigma_{t'}|_W differs from sigma_t|_W for every t' > t; in particular a vertex that switches alone never switches again, and a sub-game that runs in isolation for one round can never be reset to that local configuration.
results.argument: cor:no-return gives Delta(sigma_t, sigma_{t'}) meet S_t nonempty, and S_t is contained in W, so the two strategies differ somewhere on W. For (i) take W = {v} and use that v has two actions.
results.verification: It IS cor:no-return restated, exactly as the task suspected: the proof is one line and uses nothing else. VERDICT: INTEGRATE, but AS A COROLLARY of cor:no-return with the one-line proof (drafted in the LaTeX), not as a lemma. Its content is the two readings (i) and (ii), which are worth keeping.

results.name: allswlower:cor-selfread (a self-reading vertex switches exactly at its loop value)
results.statement: On a ONE-PLAYER stopping SSG with sigma, p in Vmax, a = sigma(p), b = sigma-bar(p), h = h(b->p) and ell the value of b conditioned on never visiting p: h < 1, val_sigma(b) = h val_sigma(a) + (1-h) ell, p is strictly switchable at sigma iff ell > val_sigma(a), and then val_{sigma[p]}(p) = ell.
results.argument: h < 1 is the second paragraph of thm:impedance's proof (a chain returning to p with probability one is never absorbed) -- so it is a CONCLUSION, not a hypothesis. Conditioning at the first visit to p, with val_sigma(p) = val_sigma(a), gives the decomposition. Since 1-h > 0 the decomposition makes val_sigma(b) > val_sigma(a) equivalent to ell > val_sigma(a). thm:impedance at v = p, where h(p->p)=1, gives val_{sigma[p]}(p) - val_sigma(a) = (val_sigma(b)-val_sigma(a))/(1-h) = ell - val_sigma(a).
results.verification: selfread.py: 1028 (game, sigma, p) triples over random one-player stopping SSGs, all three conclusions exact, 0 failures. REPAIR: the hypothesis 'p is not reachable from a under sigma' is NEVER USED and should be DELETED -- 269 of those 1028 triples VIOLATE it and satisfy all three conclusions. The hypothesis 'h < 1' should likewise move from the hypotheses to the conclusions. VERDICT: INTEGRATE with both hypotheses removed (the statement is strictly stronger, and the remark allswlower:rem-laws that uses it is unaffected).

results.name: las2:thm-two (the degree-two lift is exact at |C| <= 2)
results.statement: The degree-two Lasserre relaxation L_1(G) of las2:def-relax is exact on every stopping SSG with |C| <= 2, with no nondegeneracy hypothesis.
results.argument: Proof re-derived line by line and correct. I re-verified the expansion identity: for M the moment matrix and S := Y - u u^T, the constraint alpha-tilde^{v,0T} M alpha-tilde^{v,1} = 0 is exactly a_{v,0}(u) a_{v,1}(u) + alpha^{v,0T} S alpha^{v,1} = 0; with u in Q-tilde the first summand is >= 0, giving alpha^{v,0T} S alpha^{v,1} <= 0. Writing S as a Gram matrix and using las2:lem-rows (p^{v,i}_v < 1), the sign is that of <x_v - Y_v, x_v - Z_v> with Y_v, Z_v in the convex hull of the other x_j together with x_0 = 0; bilinearity reduces to the vertices. At c = 2 the vertex values at v=1 are A, A-g, A+B-2g with the first and third nonnegative, so A=0 or A<=g or x_1=x_2, and dually at v=2; if A<=g and B<=g then g>0 unless A=B=0, and Cauchy-Schwarz forces A=B=g, i.e. x_1=x_2. In each surviving case (x_1=x_2, x_1=0, x_2=0) the two products are computed to be >= 0, hence 0; then a_{v,0}(u) a_{v,1}(u) = 0 with u in Q-tilde says Tu = u, so u = w*|_C by thm:contraction.
results.verification: Proof checked; corroborated by sampling over exact 2x2 PSD S and admissible rows (las2two.py: 3563 hits at c=1 and 19 at c=2 with all products <= 0, every one of them with BOTH products exactly 0; c=3 random sampling produces 0 hits, which is uninformative and is exactly why las2:rem-c3's engineered configuration is needed). REPAIR OF THE READING: the task's phrasing 'exact iff |C| <= 2' is NOT a theorem and must not be written. Exactness holds at |C| = 3 and 4 on CYC(3,lambda,W) and CYC(4,lambda,W) for every lambda, by las2:thm-cyc(a). What is sharp is the UNIFORM statement: exact on every stopping SSG with |C| <= 2, and false on some stopping SSG with |C| = 3 (thm:lasserre-vacuous). VERDICT: INTEGRATE the theorem; REPAIR the 'iff' reading.

results.name: las2:lem-local (the local criterion) and las2:thm-w10 / las2:thm-w14
results.statement: (a) If (u,Y) in L_1 has u != w*|_C then X := (Y-uu^T) + udot udot^T is PSD, nonzero, and alpha_v^T X beta_v = -gamma_v theta_v with theta_v = s_v alpha_v . udot >= 0, udot = A^{-1}(s .* theta), theta != 0. (b) Conversely, from X > 0 with alpha_v^T X beta_v <= 0 for all v and < 0 for some v one builds (u_t, Y_t) in L_1 with u_t != w*|_C.
results.argument: (a) Using a_{v,sigma(v)}(w*) = 0 one has a_{v,sigma(v)}(u) = alpha_v.udot and a_{v,1-sigma(v)}(u) = s_v gamma_v + beta_v.udot; substituting into the constraint and adding (alpha_v.udot)(beta_v.udot) gives alpha_v^T X beta_v = -(alpha_v.udot) s_v gamma_v = -theta_v gamma_v. (b) tX - t^2 udot udot^T is PSD for t <= (udot^T X^{-1} udot)^{-1}, and the computation of (a) run backwards gives the equalities exactly: the coefficient of t is theta_v gamma_v + f_v = 0.
results.verification: las2w.py: W_10 and W_14 rebuilt from their graphs; w* by brute force = (1/2,1/2,1/4,1/2,1/4,7/16,3/8,1/4) and (1/2,1/2,15/32) on the controlled vertices, exactly as printed; harmonic normal forms exactly as printed; gamma = (1/4,1/16,3/16) on W_10; the printed (u,Y) verified to lie in L_1 exactly (moment matrix PSD by exact LDL, box, Q-tilde, all three equalities exactly 0) with S positive definite. las2:lem-local(a) checked on both witnesses (X PSD, alpha^T X beta = -gamma*theta exactly, theta >= 0 and nonzero, udot = A^{-1}(s.*theta)); (b) checked by rebuilding a fresh witness at t = 1/4 from X on both games. VERDICT: INTEGRATE (these two theorems are already in the paper as thm:lasserre-vacuous; the verification confirms them and the engine).

results.name: las2:thm-cyc (the spectral criterion on CYC) and las2:prop-rlt, las2:prop-cyc-rlt
results.statement: On CYC(c,lambda,W) the degree-two relaxation is exact iff min_k psi_lambda(cos 2pi k/c) >= 0, where psi_lambda(t) = 2 lambda^2 t^2 - 2 lambda t + 1 - lambda^2. Consequently it is exact at c = 3,4 for every lambda and fails for every c >= 6 at lambda = 3/4 and every c >= 5 at lambda = 15/16. One RLT round R(G) is exact on W_10 and NOT on W_14, where max x(v_i) = 25/42, 7/12, 9/16. And for lambda <= lambda_0 = 0.754877... (the root of l^3+l^2=1) the local system of las2:lem-rlt-local is unsolvable on CYC(c,lambda,W) for every c and W, so L_1^+ is exact there.
results.argument: Averaging a witness over the cyclic shift makes X a PSD circulant with X_{i,i} - 2 lambda X_{i,i+1} + lambda^2 X_{i,i+2} = (1/c) sum_k mu_k psi_lambda(cos theta_k); this is the criterion, and E_k + eps I realises it. For prop-cyc-rlt: alpha_v^T X alpha_w = g_{v-w} with g_m = (1/c) sum nu_k cos(m theta_k), nu_k = mu_k G(theta_k) >= 0, G(theta) = |1 - lambda e^{i theta}|^2; Phi = psi_lambda(cos .)/G = Re((1-lambda z)/(1-lambda z-bar)) expands as (1-l^2) - l^3 cos theta + (1-l^2) sum_{n>=2} l^n cos n theta (I re-derived this expansion); the second constraint family says g_m >= 0 for all m, so -gamma theta_0 >= (1-l^2) g_0 - l^3 g_1 >= (1 - l^2 - l^3) g_0 >= 0 using g_1 <= g_0, forcing theta = 0.
results.verification: las2cyc.py, las2w.py, las2rlt.py. CYC verified stopping with w* == W, gamma_i = W(1-lambda), first action optimal. Part (a)'s four psi evaluations are exact identities. The criterion's exact/fail pattern reproduced for c = 3..15 at lambda = 3/4 (exact up to c=5, fails from c=6) and lambda = 15/16 (fails from c=5). EXPLICIT RATIONAL witnesses (u_t, Y_t) built by las2:lem-local(b) and verified to lie in L_1 exactly for CYC(6,3/4,1/2), CYC(7,3/4,1/2), CYC(5,15/16,1/2) and, freshly, CYC(9,3/4,1/2) and CYC(12,3/4,1/4). las2:prop-rlt reproduced by exact two-phase simplex over R(G) with all 4|C| rows and all their pairwise products: W_10 gives (1/2,1/2), (1/2,1/2), (1/4,1/4) -- exact -- and W_14 gives max (25/42, 7/12, 9/16) and min (1/2, 1/2, 15/32), exactly as printed. las2:prop-cyc-rlt corroborated by an exact LP OUTER relaxation (X's PSD constraint dropped, so infeasibility is a proof): infeasible for every c = 3..7 and lambda in {1/2, 3/4, 19/25, 7/8, 15/16, 31/32, 63/64}, including 19/25 > lambda_0. TWO REPAIRS: (b) 'min over [-1,1] of psi_lambda = 1/2 - lambda^2 attained at t = 1/(2 lambda)' holds only for lambda >= 1/2 (at lambda = 1/4 the minimum on [-1,1] is 9/16 at t = 1); the conclusion is unaffected. (c) the printed roots t_pm = 1/(2l) +- sqrt(2l^2-1)/(sqrt2 l) are wrong by a factor sqrt2 -- the discriminant is 4 l^2 (2l^2-1), so t_pm = 1/(2l) +- sqrt(2l^2-1)/(2l); the printed numerical arcs were computed from the CORRECT formula (25.53, 64.47, width 38.94 at l=3/4, matching '25.5, 64.5, 39.0'), except that at l = 15/16 the arc is (3.96 deg, 86.04 deg) of width 82.08, not (3.7, 86.0) of width 82.4. VERDICT: INTEGRATE all four with those two formula repairs.

results.name: cor:prec-characterisation (the escape class, intrinsically)
results.statement: A family carries escape certificates with log_2(1/lambda) >= 1/poly(N) and log_2 kappa = poly(N) if and only if 1 - Lambda(G) >= 1/poly(N), where Lambda = max over the 2^{|C|} profiles of rho(M_pi).
results.argument: (=>) is thm:prec-rate(i) (Collatz-Wielandt). (<=) With Lambda <= 1 - 1/p take lambda := 1 - 1/(3p); then lambda^2 >= 1 - 2/(3p) >= Lambda so rho(A_pi) = rho(M_pi)/lambda <= lambda < 1, and the certificate x = (I-A_pi)^{-1} 1 of thm:prec-rate(ii) has kappa(x) <= ||x||_inf, bounded by Cramer with |det(I-A_pi)| >= (1-lambda)^n (every eigenvalue of A_pi has modulus <= lambda) and Hadamard on the cofactors; the log is polynomial because log_2 1/(1-lambda) = log_2(3p). Then log_2(1/lambda) >= 1/(3p) and thm:escape-class applies.

\begin{lemma}[Same-successor bias]\label{bsr:lem-bias}
Let $v\in\Vmax$ have successors $p\in\Vmax$ and $q\in\Vavg$ with the same
successor pair $\{a,b\}$, as every $v_i$ of the ladder $L_n$ of
\Cref{thm:ladder} has. Then for every Min strategy $\tau$,
$\val^\tau(p)\ge\val^\tau(q)$, with equality if and only if
$\val^\tau(a)=\val^\tau(b)$. Hence the strict variant of \Cref{def:bsi} never
endorses the switch of $v$ from $p$ to $q$, and the non-strict variant
endorses it only when $\val^\tau(a)=\val^\tau(b)$, while the switch from $q$
to $p$ is endorsed whenever it is improving. Moreover the switch $p\to q$ is
$\val_\sigma$-improving at $v$ if and only if $p$ itself is strictly
switchable at $\sigma$. Dually at $\Vmin$ with $\val_\sigma$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\val^\tau$ is the value of the one-player game in which Min is frozen to
$\tau$, so it is the least fixed point of $T^\tau$ and satisfies
$\val^\tau(p)=\max\{\val^\tau(a),\val^\tau(b)\}$ at the Max vertex $p$ and
$\val^\tau(q)=\tfrac12(\val^\tau(a)+\val^\tau(b))$ at the average vertex $q$;
a maximum dominates a mean, with equality only when the two arguments agree.
The veto for $p\to q$ at $v$ reads $\val^\tau(q)\ge\val^\tau(p)$ (resp.\ $>$),
and the veto for $q\to p$ reads $\val^\tau(p)\ge\val^\tau(q)$, which always
holds. For the last claim, $\val_\sigma(p)=\val_\sigma(\sigma(p))$ and
$\val_\sigma(q)=\tfrac12(\val_\sigma(a)+\val_\sigma(b))$ with
$\sigma(p)\in\{a,b\}$, so $\val_\sigma(q)>\val_\sigma(p)$ if and only if
$\val_\sigma(\bar\sigma(p))>\val_\sigma(\sigma(p))$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Self-dual games: BSI is a one-sided rule]\label{bsr:prop-selfdual}
Let $G$ be stopping and \emph{self-dual}: there is an involution $\phi$ of $V$
with $\phi(t_0)=t_1$, $\phi(\Vmax)=\Vmin$, $\phi(\Vavg)=\Vavg$ and
$\phi(x^{(i)})=\phi(x)^{(i)}$ for every non-sink $x$, so that $\phi$ is an
isomorphism of $G$ onto its dual $\bar G$. For a Max strategy $\sigma$ let
$\phi(\sigma)$ be the Min strategy $\phi(v)\mapsto\phi(\sigma(v))$. Then
\[
  \val^{\phi(\sigma)}(x)=1-\val_\sigma(\phi(x))\qquad (x\in V,\ \text{sinks included}),
\]
and from a mirrored pair $(\sigma,\phi(\sigma))$ every BSI round produces a
mirrored pair, with $C_{\min}=\phi(C_{\max})$ and
\[
  C_{\max}=\bigl\{v\in S_\sigma:\ \val_\sigma(\phi(\bar\sigma(v)))\le
  \val_\sigma(\phi(\sigma(v)))\bigr\}
\]
($<$ for the strict variant). So on self-dual games from mirrored starts BSI
is the one-sided rule $\mathrm{MR}\colon\sigma\mapsto\sigma[C_{\max}]$, which
reads $\val_\sigma$ and $\phi$ only; by \Cref{thm:bsi-nostall} it returns a
nonempty subset of $S_\sigma$ whenever $S_\sigma\ne\emptyset$, so it is a
switching rule in the sense of \Cref{def:rule}. It endorses the switch of $v$
to $q$ exactly when Min's best response to $\sigma$ at the mirror vertex
$\phi(v)$ weakly (resp.\ strictly) prefers $\phi(q)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Freezing Min to $\phi(\sigma)$ in $G$ leaves a Max-only stopping game; its
dual is a Min-only stopping game which $\phi$ carries isomorphically onto
$G_\sigma$, the game with Max frozen to $\sigma$. \Cref{lem:duality} gives
$\val^{\phi(\sigma)}=1-\val_\sigma\circ\phi$ off the sinks, and at the sinks
both sides read $1$ at $t_1$ and $0$ at $t_0$ because $\phi$ exchanges them.
Substituting $U=1-L\circ\phi$ with $L=\val_\sigma$ in \Cref{def:bsi}:
$u=\phi(v)$ lies in $S^{\phi(\sigma)}$ iff $U(\phi\bar\sigma(v))<U(\phi\sigma(v))$
iff $L(\bar\sigma(v))>L(\sigma(v))$ iff $v\in S_\sigma$; and the Min veto
$L(\bar\tau(u))\le L(\tau(u))$ reads $L(\phi\bar\sigma(v))\le L(\phi\sigma(v))$,
which is the Max veto $U(\bar\sigma(v))\ge U(\sigma(v))$ at $v$. Hence
$C_{\min}=\phi(C_{\max})$ and $\tau[C_{\min}]=\phi(\sigma[C_{\max}])$, so the
new pair is mirrored again. The last sentence restates the veto:
$L(\phi q)\le L(\phi p)$ says that $\phi(q)$ attains
$\min\{L(\phi p),L(\phi q)\}=L(\phi v)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Normalisation preserves BSI]\label{bsr:prop-normal}
Let $N'(G)$ be the bipartite normal form of \Cref{lem:normalform} and
$\sigma\mapsto\tilde\sigma$, $\tau\mapsto\tilde\tau$ its bijections on the two
strategy sets. Then $\val^{N'(G)}_{\tilde\sigma}=\val^{G}_\sigma$ and
$\val_{N'(G)}^{\tilde\tau}=\val_{G}^{\tau}$ on $V(G)$, both taking at the two
gadget vertices replacing an edge $(v,u)$ the value of $u$; consequently
$S_{\tilde\sigma}=S_\sigma$, $S^{\tilde\tau}=S^\tau$,
$C_{\max}(\tilde\sigma,\tilde\tau)=C_{\max}(\sigma,\tau)$ and
$C_{\min}(\tilde\sigma,\tilde\tau)=C_{\min}(\sigma,\tau)$ for both variants,
so the BSI runs on $(G,\sigma_0,\tau_0)$ and on
$(N'(G),\tilde\sigma_0,\tilde\tau_0)$ have the same length and pass through
corresponding pairs. The same holds for the $k$-blinding normalisation $N_k$
of \Cref{def:kblind}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{lem:normalform}(iii) is the statement for $\val_\sigma$. The gadget
$v\to c_{v,u}$, $c_{v,u}\to(u,d_{v,u})$, $d_{v,u}\to(u,c_{v,u})$ uses only
average vertices and is inserted at exactly the edges whose two endpoints are
controlled, a condition invariant under exchanging the players and the sinks;
hence $N'(\bar G)=\overline{N'(G)}$ under the same vertex naming, and
\Cref{lem:normalform}(iii) applied to $\bar G$, carried back by
\Cref{lem:duality}, is the statement for $\val^\tau$. Each of the four tests
of \Cref{def:bsi} compares two numbers that are therefore unchanged. For

\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The law bound]\label{deg:prop-g}
Let $g(m)$ be the greatest $L$ such that some sequence
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ in $\{0,1\}^{m}$ with
$S_t:=\sigma_t\oplus\sigma_{t+1}\ne\emptyset$ for $t<L$ and $S_L:=\emptyset$
obeys \Cref{cor:no-return}, \Cref{cor:law-b} and \Cref{cor:law-u}. Then
$g(m)=1,2,4,7,12$ for $m=1,\dots,5$ and $g(6)=21$, so that
$h^{\ast}(m)\le g(m)\le f(m)$ with $g(5)=h^{\ast}(5)=12<13=f(5)$ and
$g(6)=21<25=f(6)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
All three laws are invariant under translation of the cube and under
permutation of the coordinates, so $\sigma_0=0$ and $S_0=\{1,\dots,k\}$ may be
assumed. The sequences are built left to right by depth-first search:
choosing $S_t$ requires $(\sigma_u\oplus\sigma_t)\not\subseteq S_t$
(\Cref{cor:law-b}) and $(S_u\bigtriangleup S_t)\cap(\sigma_u\oplus\sigma_t)\ne
\emptyset$ (\Cref{cor:law-u}) for every $u<t$, and setting
$\sigma_{t+1}:=\sigma_t\oplus S_t$ requires
$(\sigma_u\oplus\sigma_{t+1})\cap S_u\ne\emptyset$ for every $u\le t$
(\Cref{cor:no-return}); between them these tests cover every pair the three
laws constrain, since \Cref{cor:law-u} at $t'=L$ is \Cref{cor:no-return}. The
search is exhaustive. $h^{\ast}\le g$ because a bottom-antipodal trace obeys
all three laws (\Cref{lem:auso-laws}, \Cref{cor:law-u}), and $g\le f$ because
\Cref{cor:law-u} is an extra constraint.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Damping cannot remove a tie at value zero]\label{deg:prop-zeroties}
Let $G$ be an SSG and let $G^{\flat}$ be obtained by replacing each edge
$u\to w$ by a damping chain (\Cref{def:damping}) of an arbitrary,
edge-dependent length $k_e\ge0$, so that the edge delivers $w$ with
probability $1-2^{-k_e}$ and $t_0$ with probability $2^{-k_e}$. Then for every
Max strategy $\sigma$
\[
  \{v\in V(G):\val^{G^{\flat}}_\sigma(v)=0\}
  =\{v\in V(G):\val^{G}_\sigma(v)=0\}=Z_\sigma ,
\]
the trapping set of \Cref{def:trap}, which depends on the digraph of $G$ and
on $\sigma$ only and on no probability. Consequently every incidence
$(\sigma,i)$ tied at the value $0$ in $G$ stays tied in $G^{\flat}$, whatever
the $k_e$; in particular no such perturbation makes $B'$ of
\Cref{prop:overshoot-small} nondegenerate, all ten of its ties being ties at
the value $0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:trap} the zero set of $\val_\sigma$ is the greatest
$\sigma$-trap, so it suffices to show that the greatest $\sigma$-trap
$Z^{\flat}$ of $G^{\flat}$ meets $V(G)$ in the greatest $\sigma$-trap $Z$ of
$G$. Write $c^{e}_1,\dots,c^{e}_{k_e}$ for the chain of $e=(u\to w)$, so that
$c^e_i\to(w,c^e_{i+1})$ for $i<k_e$ and $c^e_{k_e}\to(w,t_0)$; all are
average, and $k_e=0$ means the edge is unchanged.

($\supseteq$) Put $U:=Z\cup\{c^e_i: e=(u\to w)\text{ with }w\in Z\}$; note
$t_0\in Z$, since $t_0$ has no successors and $Z$ is the greatest set with the
closure properties. An average $c^e_i\in U$ has both successors in $U$ ($w\in
Z$ and $c^e_{i+1}$, or $t_0\in Z$); an average $v\in Z$ has both its
$G$-successors in $Z$, hence both chain heads in $U$; a Max $v\in Z$ has
$\sigma(v)\in Z$, hence the head of that edge's chain in $U$; a Min $v\in Z$
has some successor in $Z$, hence that chain's head in $U$. And $t_1\notin U$.
So $U$ is a $\sigma$-trap of $G^{\flat}$ and $Z\subseteq Z^{\flat}$.

($\subseteq$) Put $W:=Z^{\flat}\cap V(G)$. If $v\in W$ is average, both chain
heads $c^e_1$ lie in $Z^{\flat}$; an average vertex of a trap keeps both
successors, so the head $w$ of each of those chains lies in $Z^{\flat}$, and
both $G$-successors of $v$ lie in $W$. If $v\in W$ is controlled, the same
argument applied to the chain of an edge it keeps puts that edge's head in
$W$. And $t_1\notin W$. So $W$ is a $\sigma$-trap of $G$ and $W\subseteq Z$.

Finally, if $\val^{G}_\sigma(x^{(0)})=\val^{G}_\sigma(x^{(1)})=0$ at
$x\in\Vmax$ then both heads lie in $Z$, so in $G^{\flat}$ both chain heads
carry the value $(1-2^{-k_e})\cdot0+2^{-k_e}\cdot0=0$ and the incidence is
still tied.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No return to an isolated configuration]\label{allswlower:lem-isolated}
Let $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ be an all-switches run on a stopping SSG and
$S_t=\sigma_t\oplus\sigma_{t+1}$. If $W\subseteq\Vmax$ and $S_t\subseteq W$
for some round $t$, then $\sigma_{t'}|_W\ne\sigma_t|_W$ for every $t'>t$. In
particular (i) if $S_t=\{v\}$ then $\sigma_{t'}(v)=\sigma_{t+1}(v)$ for all
$t'>t$: a vertex that switches alone never switches again; and (ii) if some
round switches only vertices of $W$, the strategy restricted to $W$ never
again equals what it was at the start of that round, so a sub-game on $W$ that
runs in isolation for a single round can never be reset to that local
configuration and re-run.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{cor:no-return} gives $\Delta(\sigma_t,\sigma_{t'})\cap S_t\ne\emptyset$,
and $S_t\subseteq W$, so the two strategies differ somewhere on $W$. For (i)
take $W=\{v\}$ and use that $v$ has two actions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A self-reading vertex switches exactly at its loop value]\label{allswlower:cor-selfread}
Let $G$ be a one-player stopping SSG, $\sigma$ a Max strategy and $p\in\Vmax$
with $a=\sigma(p)$, $b=\bar\sigma(p)$. Let $h:=h(b\to p)$ be the probability
that the $\sigma$-chain started at $b$ visits $p$; then $h<1$, and, writing
$\ell$ for the value of $b$ conditioned on never visiting $p$,
\[
  \val_\sigma(b)=h\,\val_\sigma(a)+(1-h)\,\ell ,
\]
$p$ is strictly switchable at $\sigma$ if and only if $\ell>\val_\sigma(a)$,
and in that case $\val_{\sigma[p]}(p)=\ell$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
$h<1$ is the second paragraph of the proof of \Cref{thm:impedance}: if the
chain returned to $p$ from $b$ with probability one it would never be
absorbed. Starting at $b$, condition on the first visit to $p$: on that event
the strong Markov property and $\val_\sigma(p)=\val_\sigma(a)$ give
conditional absorption probability $\val_\sigma(a)$, and on its complement, by
definition, $\ell$; this is the display. Since $1-h>0$, the display makes
$\val_\sigma(b)>\val_\sigma(a)$ equivalent to $\ell>\val_\sigma(a)$. Finally
\Cref{thm:impedance} at $v=p$, where $h(p\to p)=1$, gives
$\val_{\sigma[p]}(p)-\val_\sigma(a)=(\val_\sigma(b)-\val_\sigma(a))/(1-h)
=\ell-\val_\sigma(a)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The contracted escape class]\label{thm:prec-contract-class}
There is an algorithm which, given a stopping SSG $G$ with $C\ne\emptyset$,
computes the harmonic normal form and then iterates $\widehat T$ two-sidedly
in binary fixed point with the upper iterate rounded up and the lower rounded
down to multiples of $2^{-p}$, doubling $p$ through $2,4,8,\dots$ and
restarting, stopping when the width falls below $4^{-a}$, and then returns the
rational vector of denominator at most $2^{a}$ nearest the midpoint, extended
harmonically. It always returns $\val$, whatever $p$; and if
$(\widehat\lambda,\widehat x)$ is an escape certificate for $\widehat S$ with
$\min\widehat x=1$ and $\widehat\kappa=\max\widehat x$, then at every
\[
  p\ \ge\ 2a+3+\log_2\widehat\kappa+\log_2\frac1{1-\widehat\lambda}
\]
it stops after $O\bigl((a+\log_2\widehat\kappa)/\log_2(1/\widehat\lambda)\bigr)$
rounds, so the doubling schedule costs a factor $O(1)$ in rounds and
$O(\log p)$ restarts. Consequently \Cref{prob:main} is decidable in polynomial
time on every family with $1-\widehat\Lambda(G)\ge1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$, and
that class contains the escape class of \Cref{thm:escape-class} by
\Cref{thm:prec-contract}(iii).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Directed rounding preserves $\widehat l_k\le\val|_C\le\widehat u_k$ at every
$p$, because $\widehat T$ is monotone and fixes $\val|_C$; this is what makes
the algorithm correct independently of $p$, and hence makes the doubling
schedule legitimate. It also keeps every iterate a multiple of $2^{-p}$, so
the bit size does not grow. Put $d_k:=\widehat u_k-\widehat l_k\ge0$ and
$\|y\|_{\widehat x}:=\max_v y(v)/\widehat x(v)$. Then
$d_{k+1}\le\widehat Sd_k+2^{1-p}\bbone$, and $\widehat S$ is monotone and
positively homogeneous with $\widehat S\widehat x\le\widehat\lambda\widehat x$,
so $\|\widehat Sd\|_{\widehat x}\le\widehat\lambda\|d\|_{\widehat x}$ and
$\|\bbone\|_{\widehat x}\le1$; hence
$\|d_k\|_{\widehat x}\le\widehat\lambda^{k}+2^{1-p}/(1-\widehat\lambda)$ and
\[
  \|d_k\|_\infty\ \le\ \widehat\kappa\widehat\lambda^{k}
  +\widehat\kappa\,\frac{2^{1-p}}{1-\widehat\lambda}.
\]
The second term is below $\tfrac12 4^{-a}$ exactly at the stated $p$, and the
first below $\tfrac12 4^{-a}$ after
$k\ge(2a+1+\log_2\widehat\kappa)/\log_2(1/\widehat\lambda)$ rounds. Two
distinct coordinates of $\val$ differ by at least $4^{-a}$ by
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}, so once the width is below $4^{-a}$ the midpoint
$z$ satisfies $|z(v)-\val(v)|<\tfrac12 4^{-a}\le1/(2q^{2})$ for the
denominator $q\le2^{a}$ of $\val(v)$, and $\val(v)$ is recovered by continued
fractions. The harmonic extension is \Cref{lem:transport-dim}. The certificate
exists at every rate above $\widehat\Lambda$, with
$\log_2\widehat\kappa$ polynomial, by \Cref{thm:prec-rate} and the proof of
\Cref{cor:prec-characterisation} applied to the rectangular family
$\{\widehat R_\pi\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What was repaired]\label{v14:rem-prec}
The round-14 statement set $p:=\Theta(a+\log_2\frac1{1-\widehat\Lambda})$,
which does not make the second term of the displayed width bound --- the
bound the note itself derives --- fall below $4^{-a}$: the factor

neither $\widehat\kappa$ nor $\widehat\lambda$ is available to the algorithm,

\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The wedge defeats the contraction, at the same rate]\label{prop:prec-wedge}
For $WD(e,j,m)$ of \Cref{def:wedge} the contracted matrix is
$\widehat R(v_i,a;\cdot)=0$ and $\widehat R(v_i,b;v_{3-i})=1-2^{1-j}$, so
$\widehat\Lambda(WD(e,j,m))=1-2^{1-j}$ exactly, independent of $e$ and $m$.
Hence on $WD(2j,j,j+4)$, where $N=6j+9$,
$\log_2(1/\widehat\Lambda)=2^{-\Theta(N)}$ and the family lies outside the
contracted class; whereas on $WD(e,2,m)$ with $e$ growing it lies inside,
while lying outside the escape class. Measured exactly, the two-sided
contracted iteration reaches width $0$ on $WD(2j,j,j+4)$ after
$4,8,17,35,70,140,281$ rounds for $j=2,\dots,8$ --- the numbers of
\Cref{prop:wedge} --- and after $4$ rounds on $WD(e,2,6)$ for every
$e=2,\dots,7$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Under the $a$-branch the passage from $v_i$ returns to $v_i$ with probability
$1-2^{-e}$ and reaches $H$, hence a sink, otherwise, so the row normalisation
annihilates it. Under the $b$-branch, $b_i$ returns to $v_i$ with probability
$\tfrac12$ and enters $c_{i,1}$ otherwise, from which $v_{3-i}$ is reached
with probability $1-2^{1-j}$ and $w_1$, hence a sink, otherwise; dividing by

has one nonzero row, or is antidiagonal with both entries $1-2^{1-j}$, and
only the last has nonzero spectral radius, equal to $1-2^{1-j}$. The round
counts are measurements.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The few-denominator class does contain stalls]\label{v14:prop-fv-stall}
For $n\ge3$ let $\mathrm{FV}(n)$ and $\mathrm{FV}_2(n)$ be the families of
\Cref{prop:fv-family}, which have $D(G)=3$ and are therefore solved by
\Cref{thm:few-denominator} in $O(N^{2})$ operations. Seeded with $Z_0,Z_1$ and
read in both directions of \Cref{rem:own-successor} at every controlled
vertex, the slack calculus of \Cref{def:slack} and its min-plus transitive
closure of \Cref{def:trans-slack} \emph{never} fire on them, at any round; nor
does the one-shot transport test of \Cref{def:transport} over $Q(G;Z_0,Z_1)$.
By contrast the value-simulation preorder of \Cref{def:simorder} decides every
controlled vertex, and the seeded transport-slack hybrid of \Cref{sec:hybrid}
decides every controlled vertex at round two or three.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Every controlled vertex of $\mathrm{FV}(n)$ and $\mathrm{FV}_2(n)$ has two
successors of equal value, so only direction (i) of
\Cref{rem:own-successor} --- an upper bound $\Delta_k(v,v^{(i)})\le0$ on a
difference that is exactly $0$ --- is available, and firing requires
$\Delta_k$ to \emph{attain} $0$. Write $W(x,y):=w^\ast(x)-w^\ast(y)$ and let
$F$ be one round of the mechanism. Soundness of the calculus is
$D\ge W\Rightarrow F(D)\ge W$; in particular $F(W)\ge W$. Every entry of
$F(D)$ is a minimum of finitely many expressions each of which is a constant
or a maximum, minimum, mean or (for the closure) min-plus path sum of entries
of $D$. Fix a $0/1$ matrix $\Psi$ and consider $D=W+c\Psi$: each such
expression is piecewise affine in $c$, and its breakpoints occur where two
attainable $W$-combinations differ divided by the difference of two attainable
$\Psi$-combinations. On $\mathrm{FV}(n)$ and $\mathrm{FV}_2(n)$ every value of
$w^\ast$ lies in $\{0,\tfrac13,\tfrac23,1\}$, so every attainable
$W$-combination is a multiple of $\tfrac16$, while every attainable
$\Psi$-combination lies in $[0,N]$; hence no breakpoint lies in
$(0,\tfrac1{6N})$ and
\[
  F(W+c\Psi)=F(W)+c\,\Theta \qquad\bigl(0<c<\tfrac1{6N}\bigr)
\]
for a matrix $\Theta$ independent of $c$. Run the mechanism $K=14$ rounds from
$D_0\equiv\bbone$, put $S:=\{(x,y):D_K(x,y)>W(x,y)\}$, $\Psi:=\mathbf 1_S$ and
$t:=\min\{\min_{S}(D_K-W),\ \tfrac1{12N}\}>0$. Three finite exact checks ---
$F(W)\ge W$, $\Theta\ge\tfrac12\Psi$, and $D_K\ge W+t\Psi$ --- then give, by
induction, $D_{K+j}\ge W+t2^{-j}\Psi$ for every $j$, so $D_k>W$ on $S$ for
ever. All four entries the test reads at each controlled vertex either lie in
$S$ with $W=0$ there (the two ``$\le0$'' entries, which therefore stay
strictly positive) or have $W\ge0$ (the two ``$<0$'' entries, which are
bounded below by $W\ge0$). Hence neither direction ever fires. The three
checks were carried out in exact arithmetic for $n=3,4,5,6$ and both variants,
and the transport, preorder and hybrid statements are exact computations.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The sentence \Cref{thm:few-denominator} was missing]\label{v14:rem-fewden}
\Cref{rem:escape-class} records that no member of the escape class can stall
the propagation mechanisms of \Cref{sec:gap}. The corresponding sentence for
\Cref{thm:few-denominator} is the opposite one, and it is worth stating
because the reason is instructive: \emph{the few-denominator class does
contain stalling instances for \textup{M2}, \textup{M2T} and \textup{M4}, and
they are stalls of the degenerate kind}. On $\mathrm{FV}(n)$, $n\ge3$, no
controlled vertex is value-distinguishing, so the strict direction (ii) of
\Cref{rem:own-successor} can never fire and the non-strict direction (i)
requires an exact zero which a geometrically converging upper bound never
attains: \Cref{v14:prop-fv-stall} shows both calculi are silent for ever,
$\Delta_k(X_0,L_0)=2^{-\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor}$ on $\mathrm{FV}(3)$. This is
the sharpest illustration in this document of the point
\Cref{prop:fv-family} makes about ``easy in a stronger sense than membership
of a class'': the sentence there --- that every sound decision rule settles
these vertices at once --- is true of a rule that is told the two successors
have equal value, and false of the calculi, which have to derive it. The
class therefore does \emph{not} lie on the easy side of every mechanism, and
the sentence to attach to \Cref{thm:few-denominator} is this: \emph{unlike the
escape class, the few-denominator class contains stalls of \textup{M2},
\textup{M2T} and \textup{M4}; but every stall it is known to contain is
vacuous, in that no controlled vertex of the instance is value-distinguishing,
so the decision the mechanism fails to make carries no information.} Whether
it contains a stall with a value-distinguishing vertex is open, and it is a
genuinely different question: on a family with $D(G)=\mathrm{poly}(N)$ every
value gap is at least $1/D(G)\ge1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$, but that alone bounds
nothing, since \Cref{thm:slack-vi-upper} converts a gap into a firing round
only through the two-sided value-iteration width, whose rate
\Cref{thm:contraction} bounds by $(1-2^{-a})^{k/N}$ and which $D(G)$ does not
control. \textbf{GAP:} \emph{exhibit a stopping SSG with
$D(G)=\mathrm{poly}(N)$ carrying a value-distinguishing controlled vertex on
which the $Z$-seeded own-successor test for the hybrid of \Cref{sec:hybrid} is
silent for superpolynomially many rounds, or prove that none exists.}
\end{remark}
